facts.reason: Reconciled quantity is necessary for every domestic closure, but alone establishes neither authorized route.
Reconciliation and valid handover require the remaining class-specific route conditions and absence of an active hold.
Cleared settlement is necessary for routine closure but not for the exception route.
For these current-policy snapshots, a waiver plus either completed audit or independent second inspection suffices with the unchanged common prerequisites.
Current snapshots require receiving-lead handover validity; the historical driver-signature card has no current authority.
The settlement flag references unavailable SI-9; no authoritative mapping from Y to cleared settlement is supplied.
The paid_at semantic definition and migration mapping are missing, so neither event-date mapping is established.
Largest numerical contribution is arithmetic attribution, not evidence establishing causality.
Administrative closure does not authorize payment; payment is governed by a separate unsupplied policy.
CR-17 replaces only the audit condition with an alternative and explicitly retains the waiver.
Receipt records bank arrival of funds, whereas posting records ledger entry; the dates can differ.
An active hold forbids closure even with all positive route conditions present.

decisions.reason: The routine snapshot supplies reconciled quantity, valid handover, cleared settlement and an explicitly inactive hold.
Routine cleared settlement is unavailable; Y has no supplied authoritative mapping. Exception waiver and audit cannot substitute for routine settlement.
Reconciliation, handover, waiver, independent inspection and inactive hold establish the current exception route despite false audit and settlement.
The exception audit route is established with reconciliation, valid handover, waiver and inactive hold; second inspection is unnecessary.
The explicitly false waiver defeats both current exception alternatives even though audit and inspection are true.
The explicitly active hold prohibits closure despite otherwise complete routine conditions.
Routine positive conditions are supplied, but unavailable hold status does not establish permission or a prohibition.
Audit is explicitly false but independent inspection is unavailable, leaving the alternative exception route unresolved.
Both audit and independent inspection are explicitly false, defeating all authorized exception alternatives.
Valid handover is explicitly false; a driver signature cannot satisfy the current handover requirement.
Cleared settlement is unavailable; receipt and posting dates describe events but do not establish the required cleared-settlement attestation.
Reconciliation, an unchanged necessary prerequisite, is explicitly false.
Reconciliation, valid handover, waiver, independent inspection and inactive hold establish the inspection alternative despite unavailable audit.
Reconciliation, valid handover, waiver, audit and inactive hold establish the audit alternative despite unavailable inspection.
Cleared settlement is explicitly false, violating a necessary routine closure condition.
Handover validity is unavailable; the routine route is not established, but no necessary condition is explicitly false and the hold is inactive.
